criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-core -p athena-cli`. A new test shows a Pages run that concludes `timed_out` after a merge is re-run exactly once via the gh wrapper and the run then succeeds. The test asserts that exactly one re-run call was made and that one report line names the run and the conclusion.
criteria.evidence: I ran it and `a_timed_out_pages_run_is_re_run_once_and_then_succeeds` passes. It asserts `rerun_calls() == 1`, checks that the call goes to `repos/example/project/actions/runs/5/rerun` through `GhClient`, checks that the report ends with conclusion `success` and `reruns == 1`, and checks that exactly one line contains both "run 5" and "timed_out".

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test -p athena-cli`. A new test shows a Pages run concluding `cancelled` is re-run once, and that a second failure of the re-run is reported and not re-run again (no loop).
criteria.evidence: `a_cancelled_pages_run_is_re_run_once_and_a_second_failure_is_not_re_run` passes. It asserts one re-run call, `reruns == 1`, a final conclusion of `timed_out`, one line naming run 5 and `cancelled`, and one line containing `timed_out` and "not re-running".

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. A test shows a Pages run that concludes `success` is not re-run, and a merge in a repository with no Pages run for the merged commit does not fail the landing.
criteria.evidence: `a_successful_pages_run_is_not_re_run` asserts zero re-runs. `a_commit_with_no_pages_run_is_not_an_error_and_nothing_is_re_run` asserts that `watch_pages` returns Ok with `run: None` and writes a single report line. Both tests call `watch_pages` directly. In `Athena::land_pr` (gh.rs:1280-1294), which I read but no test runs, any Err from the watch becomes a warning line and the report is still returned, so a missing run cannot fail the landing. The whole suite passed under `cargo test -q`.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo test`. The existing 5xx tests still pass: one is retried and succeeds, the other keeps failing until the three attempts run out. They cover the new Pages calls too (a 5xx on the runs listing is retried), and each retry is reported.
criteria.evidence: `operations()` now includes "list pages runs" and "re-run pages". Both `a_one_off_500_is_retried_and_succeeds_for_every_github_operation` and `persistent_500s_fail_after_three_attempts_naming_the_call_and_status` pass with these included. The new `a_5xx_on_the_runs_listing_is_retried_and_reported_during_the_watch` asserts two calls and a first report line naming HTTP 500 and pages.yml.

criteria.criterion: Run `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check`. Both are clean, and `external_calls_guard` still passes: all GitHub calls stay in crates/athena-core/src/gh.rs.
criteria.evidence: Clippy finished with no warnings. `cargo fmt --check` printed nothing. Both external_calls_guard tests pass. All new calls go through `GhClient::api` in gh.rs.

criteria.criterion: A decisions entry or doc note says how the Pages watch works: the bound on waiting, a single re-run, and that the outcome is reported to the user.
criteria.evidence: Decision D97 in docs/decisions.md and the "Watching the deploy" section in docs/design/explainer-site.md both state the wait bound (60 looks 10 s apart, about ten minutes, plus 3 looks for a run that has not appeared), the single re-run, and that every step is reported. Both match the constants and logic in gh.rs.

findings.summary: The Pages watch's wiring into `Athena::land_pr` has no test, and its sleep is hardcoded.
findings.evidence: Searching for `.land_pr(` finds only crates/athena-cli/src/main.rs, so no test runs this block. It builds its `Poll` with `std::thread::sleep` and fixed constants, so a test cannot inject them. The tests cover `watch_pages` itself, but nothing tests that a landing calls it or turns its error into a warning.

findings.summary: The Pages re-run POST is logged as the `ReadChecks` host operation.
findings.evidence: `rerun_pages` passes `HostOperation::ReadChecks` for a POST that changes state. D97 says this is on purpose because the operation list is closed, but the host-error log will call a re-run a read.

findings.summary: A 5xx on the re-run POST is retried, which can ask for the re-run twice.
findings.evidence: The re-run goes through the retrying `api` wrapper. If GitHub returns a 5xx after it has accepted the re-run, the retry sends the POST again. GitHub would most likely refuse a re-run of a run already in progress, so this is low risk. This is from reading the code; I did not test it.

findings.summary: Two expected files are untouched: crates/athena-core/src/run.rs and land.rs.
findings.evidence: The diff changes 5 of the 7 listed files and nothing outside the list. The watch lives in gh.rs instead, so there is no scope problem.

summary: The change does what the request asks, and I recommend it pass. It adds a Pages watch in gh.rs that runs after `athena land --pr` lands a pull request. The watch lists the pages.yml runs for the merged commit through the existing retrying `gh` wrapper and waits up to about ten minutes for the run to finish. It re-runs a `timed_out` or `cancelled` run once and reports each step. A second failure is reported and not re-run, and nothing in the watch can undo the landing. The tests cover a timed-out run that succeeds on its re-run, a cancelled run whose re-run also fails, a successful run, a commit with no Pages run, and a 5xx on the runs listing. The existing 5xx tests now include both new calls. I ran `cargo test -q`, the external_calls and external_calls_guard tests, `cargo clippy --all-targets` and `cargo fmt --check` on this snapshot, and all passed. D97, the explainer-site note and the CHANGELOG describe the behavior accurately. Three minor findings: no test checks that a landing actually calls the watch, and its sleep is hardcoded so a test cannot inject it; the re-run POST is logged as a read-checks operation; and a retried re-run POST could ask GitHub for the re-run twice. None of these blocks the change.
